name: Grantex
what_they_do: Open delegated authorization protocol for AI agents. OAuth 2.0 for the agentic era: principals grant agents scoped, time-limited permissions via signed JWT tokens. Every action auditable. Instant revocation including cascade across delegation chains.
positioning: Standards-track OAuth extension for agent authorization
status: Production-ready. SOC 2 Type I certified. Security audited (Vestige Security Labs). IETF Internet-Draft submitted to OAuth Working Group.

differentiation.vs_pp: JWT-scoped grants (OAuth model) vs cryptographic action receipts (PP model). Grantex is about what an agent CAN do (pre-auth); PP is about proving what an agent DID (audit trail + enforcement). Both solve authorization vacuum but at different layers.
pp_advantages: Receipt-first model: every action gets a cryptographic proof before execution
Fail-closed design (no receipt = action blocked at runtime)
Human approval gates with founder veto
More focused on audit/compliance receipts vs token delegation
Simpler mental model: receipts not OAuth grants
grantex_advantages: Standards-track (IETF) — this is a moat if OAuth WG adopts it
More integrations (LangChain, OpenAI, Google ADK, CrewAI, MCP)
More mature (679 tests, Helm chart, Terraform provider)

action: MONITOR — watch IETF draft progress. If it gains traction in OAuth WG, PP needs a standards position. Consider engaging with the author (mishrasanjeev on GitHub). Do NOT ignore — they are further along on enterprise readiness.
notes: HN post from 2026-03-03. Only 2 points which is surprisingly low for this level of work — suggests limited organic traction despite solid engineering.
